skill.name: seedance-v2
skill.description: Generate short cinematic videos with ByteDance Seedance 2.0 Pro through the RunComfy CLI. The skill explains when to use the model, how to format multimodal inputs, and how to create lip-synced clips with image, video, and audio references.
skill.summary: Create 4 to 15 second Seedance 2.0 Pro videos with RunComfy, including multimodal references and native audio.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation for using the RunComfy CLI with Seedance 2.0 Pro. I confirmed the disclosed external command and RunComfy network dependency, but found no evidence of shell injection, path traversal, hidden file abuse, prompt injection, or covert data exfiltration in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution submits prompts and media references to RunComfy.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the provider, command, required account, and outbound endpoint disclosure prominent before any invocation instructions.

remediation.issue: Users may include private images, videos, audio, or prompts in model requests.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short privacy reminder that user-provided media URLs and prompts are processed by RunComfy and should not contain sensitive data unless approved.

content.value_statement: Short-form video prompts can be hard to structure for multimodal generation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users through Seedance 2.0 Pro inputs, routing, and RunComfy CLI execution.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Seedance 2.0 Pro is the right model for a video request.
Documents the RunComfy CLI command for the Seedance 2.0 Pro endpoint.
Describes supported prompt, image, video, audio, duration, resolution, and aspect ratio inputs.
Provides prompt patterns for lip-synced ads, cinematic shots, and multimodal references.
Summarizes exit codes, retry cases, token setup, and output download behavior.
limitations: It depends on the RunComfy CLI and an active RunComfy account or token.
The documented endpoint creates clips from 4 to 15 seconds only.
The playground variant is limited to 720p output.
Reference media must be provided as supported external URLs with size and duration limits.

use_cases.title: Create lip-synced product ads
use_cases.description: Use image references and a concise speaking prompt to create short spokesperson clips with native audio.

use_cases.title: Prototype cinematic story shots
use_cases.description: Combine camera direction, mood, lighting, and reference media to generate short film preview clips.

use_cases.title: Test branded video variants
use_cases.description: Use fixed references, seeds, aspect ratios, and short prompts to compare multiple creative directions.

prompt_templates.title: Basic text-to-video clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with no reference media.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Seedance 2.0 Pro to create a 5 second 720p video of a quiet cafe at golden hour. Include a slow push-in, warm light, and gentle ambience.

prompt_templates.title: Vertical spokesperson ad
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using one character image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Seedance 2.0 Pro for a 9:16, 8 second product ad. Use this character image as the identity reference and make the person explain the offer in a warm tone.

prompt_templates.title: Multimodal scene match
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using image, video, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an 8 second Seedance clip using one subject image, one cafe video reference, and one voice reference. Match the scene mood and keep the dialogue natural.

prompt_templates.title: Variant testing plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced creative workflow across multiple outputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three Seedance 2.0 Pro variants for a 6 second brand video. Keep the same subject image, change camera motion, and recommend seeds and aspect ratios.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a short lip-synced cafe promotion using one headshot.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Seedance 2.0 Pro, suggests a 9:16 format, drafts a concise speaking prompt, and shows how to pass the image reference through RunComfy.

output_examples.input: A filmmaker wants a short preview shot with a reference location video and voice tone.
output_examples.output: The skill structures the request with scene motion, camera language, reference video, audio reference, duration, and output directory guidance.

output_examples.input: A team needs to choose between Seedance, HappyHorse, Wan, and Kling.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that Seedance is best for multimodal cinematic clips with native lip-sync, while the sibling models fit other video tasks.

best_practices: Put stable identity, costumes, logos, and visual references in image inputs instead of long text descriptions.
Use plain camera and motion language, such as slow push-in, locked wide shot, or handheld follow.
Keep clips within 4 to 15 seconds and match reference aspect ratios to the desired output.
anti_patterns: Do not combine conflicting visual styles or unrelated references in one request.
Do not ask for clips longer than the endpoint supports.
Do not place private media URLs in prompts unless RunComfy processing is approved.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you use Seedance 2.0 Pro on RunComfy to create short cinematic videos with optional image, video, and audio references.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow uses the RunComfy CLI with either browser login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN environment variable.

faq.question: Can it create long videos?
faq.answer: No. The documented endpoint supports clips from 4 to 15 seconds. Longer videos should be split into separate generations.

faq.question: Can I use reference images and audio?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents support for up to 9 images, 3 videos, and 3 audio references within the model limits.

faq.question: Is the output generated locally?
faq.answer: No. The CLI sends the request to the RunComfy model API, then downloads generated output from RunComfy URLs.

faq.question: When should I choose a different video model?
faq.answer: Choose another model when you need longer clips, motion editing on existing footage, or a different audio-driven workflow.
